text.p: This is how major world bond markets were trading in late European business on Monday.

GERMANY - German Bunds were higher late in the day, drifting in narrow ranges ahead of a three-day market holiday starting on Tuesday. Traders said there was little to no investor interest and they expected Bunds to remain around current levels when trade reopens on Friday.
The March Bund future on the London International Financial Futures and Options Exchange (LIFFE) was trading at 100.68, up 0.20 from Friday's settlement price.
BRITAIN - Gilts closed comfortably in the black, helped by a buoyant U.S. Treasury bond market.
The March gilt future settled 23/32 higher at 109-29 with nearly all those gains made after 1330 GMT. But with less than 12,000 contracts traded on the contract, volumes were very thin.

FRANCE - French bond futures ended slightly higher, supported by a positive U.S. bond market, although volume was the lowest for a session since December 26, 1995. Traders said there was little else driving French bonds besides the U.S. market and they did not expect the situation to change much before next year.
The March bond future on the MATIF in Paris settled at 128.82, up 0.06 from Friday's settlement price.
ITALY - Italian bond futures slipped back in late afternoon in very quiet pre-Christmas trade with profit-taking seen after no interest rate cut emerged following last week's inflation numbers.
The March bond future on LIFFE was trading at 128.35, down 0.25 from Friday's settlement price.

UNITED STATES - U.S. Treasuries were narrowly mixed and firmed slightly after news of November personal income and spending data. U.S. personal income rose 0.5 percent in November, slightly below economists' average forecast of a 0.6 percent gain.
The March Treasury bond future on the Chicago Board of Trade was trading at 113-16/32, up 6/32 from Friday's settlement price. The long bond was quoted to yield 6.57 percent.
JAPAN - The Tokyo market was closed for a holiday.
On Friday in after hours trading the March future on LIFFE was trading at 126.19, down 0.11 from Thursday's settlement price.

EUROBONDS - The primary market, quiet for the past couple of weeks, saw another uneventful day in the run-up to the Christmas holiday. The only excitement came from the World Bank, which brought a 20 billion peseta ($153 million) six-tranche equity-linked deal. ($1=130.8 Peseta)
